project_inclusion.note: Documented in Williamson County; local-occurrence-first inclusion.

morphology_keys.leaves: Alternate; unlobed to shallowly 3-lobed or with small toothlike lobes.
morphology_keys.sepals: About 8–9 mm at maturity with a distinctive subterminal fingerlike/awnlike projection.
morphology_keys.corolla: Small scarlet to light-scarlet, salverform/trumpet-like; limb about 12–17 mm across.
morphology_keys.key: Small scarlet flowers and awnlike sepal tips separate it quickly from the purple/blue core species.

field_diagnostics.single_best_trait: Do not stop at 'red morning glory.' Check the calyx and fruiting pedicels: the sepals carry corniform/awnlike terminal appendages, and the pedicels become reflexed beneath the fruit.
fastest_traits: Red to red-yellow salverform corolla about 20–25 mm
Outer sepals 3–3.5 mm and inner sepals 4.5–5.7 mm
Corniform/awnlike terminal appendage on the sepals
Fruiting pedicels reflexed beneath the capsule; flowering pedicels can be ascending/erect

look_alikes.distinction: FNA separates I. coccinea by reflexed fruiting pedicels (I. hederifolia remains erect in the key comparison) and larger inner sepals, 4.5–5.7 mm versus about 3–4 mm. Red flower color alone is not enough.
